briefing.opening: Good day. We begin today's Climate Change Daily Briefing for November 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🌍 COP31 and International Climate Negotiations: Mitigation Pushes and Practical Limitations
sections.content: At the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), groundbreaking measures were pursued to curb super pollutants to rein in global warming [16]. However, scientists assessed that the outcomes of COP31 reflected the reality that current efforts are failing to meet the urgent pace demanded by the climate crisis [15]. In addition, discussions are deepening over whether climate finance—essential for tackling the global crisis—should be viewed as mere 'charity' or as a 'historical obligation' of developed nations [1].

sections.title: 🔴 Escalating Climate Disasters and Cross-Border Humanitarian and Ecological Crises
sections.content: Due to the combined impacts of sea-level rise and land subsidence, an estimated 7 million coastal residents in Africa are projected to face severe flood risks by 2050 [3]. In areas such as Caparrosa in eastern Guatemala, severe drought has devastated agricultural land and displaced an increasing number of residents, yet their hopes for migration are being crushed by stringent U.S. enforcement measures [10, 17]. Furthermore, climate change is disrupting the timing of autumn bird migrations, causing widespread disturbances across natural ecosystems [11].

sections.title: ⚠️ Practical Challenges in the Energy Transition: AI Power Demand and Market Norms
sections.content: Regarding power infrastructure challenges driven by the expansion of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, concerns have been raised that renewable energy alone is insufficient to support AI data centers that require 24/7 continuous operation [8]. Amid this surging demand for carbon-free power, discussions highlight the importance of two key market signals that renewable energy contracting markets must adhere to in order to establish reliable supply chains [9]. At this critical juncture, realistic energy strategies are required to balance carbon reduction targets with the electricity demands of advanced industries [8, 9].

sections.title: 🌱 Infrastructure Adaptation and Community-Led Action Toward Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Practical efforts for climate adaptation and greenhouse gas reduction are actively underway both at home and abroad. Daesan Port is being newly developed into a climate-resilient, safe port [2], and the Korea Real Estate Board has launched public-private partnerships to advance carbon neutrality at construction sites [4]. In addition, community-centered education and public deliberation have yielded tangible results—such as Gunsan City's public-sector energy steward training [5], Jeju's youth climate action deliberative forum [6], and Sehan University's practical educator program [7]—while in Nairobi, Kenya, the National Circular Economy Strategy and Implementation Plan (CESIP 2027-2032) was officially launched [14].

briefing.closing: As the tangible damages of the climate crisis and the challenges of the energy transition become increasingly evident, we must enhance the effectiveness of international agreements and accelerate locally driven mitigation and adaptation efforts. That concludes today's climate briefing.
